summary.headline: The Tricentennial Committee discussed parade financing, time capsule logistics, and a Town Meeting zoning article allowing celebratory banners.
summary.summary: The Tricentennial Committee reviewed progress across major events planned for the town's 300th anniversary, including parade coordination, drone show contracts, and time capsule design options. Members discussed a zoning article headed to Annual Town Meeting that will permit commemorative banners on utility poles and municipal property. The committee also evaluated marketing efforts, newsletter readership, and upcoming community presentations.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved the minutes from its February 11 meeting with minor textual amendments and later voted to adjourn.
key_details: Amendments clarified committee names regarding Open Space Preservation and Breakneck Hill stewardship.
The committee voted to adjourn at the end of the agenda.
topics.outcome: Minutes approved as amended; meeting adjourned.

topics.title: Tricentennial event planning updates
topics.summary: Committee members reported on the progress of various celebratory events, focusing on parade logistics, contracts, and the town time capsule. A draft contract for the drone light show is under review by town counsel, while parade planning estimated overall expenses between $50,000 and $75,000. Members also reviewed time capsule quotes and debated whether burial should take place in July 2027 or December 2027 to capture the complete anniversary year.
key_details: Parade costs are estimated at $50,000 to $75,000, with typical participating units averaging $2,300 each.
The committee intends to request up to $25,000 in advance authorization from the supporting 501(c)(3) to begin contracting parade participants once an itemized priority budget is prepared.
The drone show contract is currently with town counsel Jay Talerman for legal review.
A deluxe time capsule and associated burial work is estimated to cost roughly $7,000, with the capsule container accounting for about $3,500.
The Knox Artillery and oxen group are not committing to parade appearances until early 2027.
topics.outcome: Draft budgets and participant priority lists will be prepared for review at the April meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: Parade commitments and celebratory contracts involve significant financial commitments and affect the town-wide 2027 celebration.

topics.title: Newsletter metrics and editorial schedule
topics.summary: The committee reviewed performance data for its digital newsletter and established a monthly deadline for event write-ups. The publication currently reaches approximately 700 recipients with a strong open rate.
key_details: The newsletter distribution list has roughly 700 subscribers with an open rate near 70 percent.
Event leads were asked to submit blurbs and updates during the last week of each month.
Newsletters will be distributed during the first week of every month.
topics.outcome: Working groups will submit promotional blurbs by the end of March for the April newsletter.

topics.title: Town Meeting zoning article for display banners
topics.summary: The committee discussed a temporary zoning warrant article drafted for the upcoming Annual Town Meeting that will allow celebratory banners across town. The Planning Board voted 4-0 in favor of the proposal, which will allow banners on municipal property, non-residential parcels, and utility poles with owner permission. The committee plans to staff an informational table at Town Meeting to answer questions and promote the celebration.
key_details: The Planning Board unanimously supported the proposed zoning article 4-0.
The article allows temporary banners for the Tricentennial on municipal property, non-residential properties, and utility poles.
Pole banners under consideration are envisioned around 12 by 18 inches, while sponsor banners could reach 6 feet wide.
A committee member will represent the article on the Town Meeting floor.
Flyers explaining the article and anniversary events will be distributed to attendees.
topics.outcome: The zoning article will go before voters at Annual Town Meeting on April 11.
topics.why_it_matters: Town Meeting approval is required to amend zoning bylaws to allow celebratory banners on utility poles and public properties throughout Southborough.

topics.title: Marketing and promotional outreach campaign
topics.summary: Members discussed a broader marketing strategy to raise public awareness and expand the committee's contact database. Outreach avenues include school take-home packets, yard signs, lawn displays, senior center publications, and partnerships with local businesses.
key_details: Marketing leads plan to utilize weekly school take-home packets to engage families.
The committee is exploring yard signs, which neighboring towns identified as their most effective marketing vehicle.
Committee representatives will present event plans at the Rotary Club meeting on March 18 at 7:00 PM at the Southborough Library.
A brick fundraiser presentation was deferred to April to coincide with the 501(c)(3) treasurer's report.
topics.outcome: Committee members will continue refining audience-specific marketing materials.

upcoming.what: Rotary Club meeting presentation at the Southborough Library
Annual Town Meeting with vote on banner zoning article
